name: math-comp
desc: Mathematical Components for the Coq proof assistant
why: A large Coq library for formal mathematics, strange and deep, though it is a proof library more than something you poke at casually.

brief.what_it_is: Mathematical Components (math-comp) is a large library of formalized mathematics written for the Coq/Rocq proof assistant, using the SSReflect proof language. It takes in Coq source files and checks them, so you get machine-verified theorems and definitions rather than program output. Its theories range from general data structures such as lists, prime numbers and finite graphs to advanced algebra. The fetched README describes it as a repository of formal theories, not an application with a user interface.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as an extensive and coherent repository of formalized mathematical theories, built to support large formal proofs. It points to two major uses: the foundations behind a formal proof of the Four Colour Theorem, and a mechanization of the Odd Order Theorem (Feit-Thompson), which uses the library extensively.
brief.how_it_works: You write proofs and definitions in Coq/Rocq using the SSReflect language and import the library's modules. The repository is organised as Coq .v files, such as ssreflect/seq.v and ssreflect/prime.v, and is installed as opam packages (rocq-mathcomp-boot, rocq-mathcomp-algebra, rocq-mathcomp-field, and others). The README does not explain the internal design further.

commands_seen.context: Adds the Rocq released opam repository so the MathComp packages can be found; the README says a fresh or up-to-date opam 2 is required.
Installs the base MathComp package via opam; other packages such as rocq-mathcomp-algebra and rocq-mathcomp-field are installed by the same pattern.

brief.install_notes: Requires opam 2 (fresh or up to date) and a working Rocq/Coq installation, both installed through opam. The base install is the two commands above; other scenarios are described in INSTALL.md, which I did not read. Nothing about hardware or accounts appeared. Help is available on Zulip, which is the primary venue for questions.
brief.standout: It is one of the few large formal libraries shown to carry real results: the README cites a formal Four Colour Theorem proof foundation and the Feit-Thompson Odd Order Theorem mechanization, a landmark result of finite group theory. The project also cites its own publications and tools built on it.
brief.status: Maintained, per the README: it says the library has been regularly released since 2008 and that new versions now come twice a year to match Rocq releases, with changes recorded in CHANGELOG.md. The README has a live pipeline badge and an active Zulip chat. I did not see a specific release date or last-commit date in the fetched text, so the exact recency is unverified.
brief.caveats: This is a proof library, not a casual tool: you need to know Coq/Rocq and SSReflect to do anything with it, so there is nothing to just run and look at. The homepage (math-comp.github.io/math-comp/) returned an empty body, so I could not read it; the README text came from the GitHub mirror page instead. Installation is via opam, and the README points to INSTALL.md for other setups, which I did not read. The README also says deprecation warnings are used between versions, so upgrades may need work.
quotes: The Mathematical Components Library is an extensive and coherent repository of formalized mathematical theories.
Recently, we have been releasing a new version twice a year, in line with the released of the Coq/Rocq proof assistant.
The primary venue for help and questions about the library nowadays is Zulip.
